MAPPINGJACOBS · LITMAP

About this companion

MappingJacobs is an interactive visual companion to Jane Jacobs’s The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961). It helps readers locate the places she mentions, read relevant excerpts, and understand how those places illustrate her arguments.

Using the map

Select a chapter to see its mapped places. Choose a marker or use place search to open an entry. You can close an entry without changing your map view. Chapter counts refer to places currently added to this companion, not to all the places mentioned in the book.

The fifteen places

This collection brings together 15 places that illustrate major themes in the book. It is an editorial selection, not a complete index or a definitive ranking. Each place has a short excerpt checked against the supplied 2016 EPUB. Explanations will be added by the project’s creator. Chapters without a selected passage remain available in the chapter list.

Excerpts and source notes

Quotations preserve Jacobs’s wording and punctuation, with whitespace normalized. Chapter references and page labels come from the working EPUB: Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group, 2016, ISBN 9780525432852. The page labels are embedded in that file; they are not screen numbers generated by an e-reader, and other editions may differ. Each passage includes its precise EPUB paragraph locator under “Edition & passage location.” Position notes distinguish an address from a representative point for a street, park or neighborhood. Checking a quotation does not establish an exact historical camera position.

Contemporary Street View

Opening a place entry automatically loads its selected panorama directly from Google. Drag to look around or open it full screen. These views show contemporary surroundings, not how a place appeared in 1961. Check the capture date and attribution inside the viewer. A checked panorama does not establish a historical match to the book. An external Google link remains available if the embedded viewer cannot load.
